title: Bounds for Homogeneous Polynomial Zeros
exact_target: Bound how many variables suffice to force a nonzero integer zero of every homogeneous polynomial of a given odd degree.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 1098 (GREEN-098). CC BY 4.0.

Amichai Lampert, Andrew Snowden and Tamar Ziegler, \emph{Polynomial Bounds for Birch’s Theorem}, arXiv:2512.00697v1 (2025), §1, definition of $N(d,s)$ and discussion of general degree bounds. For $K=\mathbb Q$, the recorded single-form threshold is $\nu(d)=N(d,1)-1$; the paper distinguishes fixed-degree dependence on the number of forms from dependence on degree.
Ben Green, \emph{100 Open Problems}, maintained author list, Problem 98 and its comments, accessed 7 October 2026.
